newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE SEEK BACK-DOOR ENTRY INTO EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE SEEK BACK-DOOR ENTRY INTO EUROPE.

text.p: Marseille, despite lying a disappointing 12th in the French first division, have not given up all hope of a place in Europe.

The 1993 European Cup winners, having held champions elect Monaco 1-1 away on Saturday, will be looking to pick up enough points in their remaining four matches starting at home against Cannes on Wednesday to qualify for the Intertoto Cup.
The four Intertoto Cup semifinalists go through to the UEFA Cup.

"Our fine performance in the principality linked to the results of our nearest rivals allow us to envisage a 10th place in the standings and possible participation in the Intertoto," coach Gerard Gili said.

Against Cannes, Gili could pick the same side that drew in Monaco, a rare occurence in a season when he has seldom been able to name an unchanged team, although midfielder Olivier Echouafni is doubtful.

Jerome Alonzo will again deputise in goal for Andreas Koepke, who missed the Monaco match with a muscle strain and has since joined the Germany squad for their World Cup qualifier at home to Ukraine on Wednesday.
Italian central defender Ivan Franceschini, veteran captain Jean-Philippe Durand and young midfielder Ludovic Asuard are still unavailable through injury.
Tunisia's Mehdi Ben Slimane, however, is back after missing the Monaco match because he was playing for his country in a World Cup qualifier.

Marseille last played in Europe in the 1994-95 season when they took part in the UEFA Cup as a second division side, having been relegated over the Valenciennes match-rigging scandal under disgraced former president Bernard Tapie.
Tapie's successor Robert Louis-Dreyfus has pledged to strengthen the squad and said anything less than fifth place in the league next season would be a failure.
Coach Gili looks like one of the most likely men to be offloaded with Bordeaux's Rolland Courbis in the frame to take his place.

Marseille, according to sources close to the club, are also after Nantes's Claude Makelele and AC MIlan's former Bordeaux striker Christophe Dugarry as well as another top French or foreign forward and libero.
Cannes coach Guy Lacombe, whose are 14th, said that playing even a relatively poor Marseille side at the Veledrome was a daunting prospect.
"Marseille, they're always a big fish with that crowd, that atmosphere. To go to Marseille, for a footballer, is always a big event. You've got to be up to it."
